title: OpenAI Revenue Run Rate Tops $40 Billion as IPO Preparations Accelerate
excerpt: The ChatGPT maker's annualized revenue has surged past $40 billion, positioning it for what could be one of the largest tech IPOs in history, even as massive cash burn and lack of profitability raise investor scrutiny.
body:
• OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate has surpassed $40 billion, up from roughly $20 billion at the end of 2025, according to reports citing company data shared with investors.
  • The company burned through $3.7 billion in Q1 2026 alone — more than half of its $5.7 billion in quarterly revenue — with full-year burn projected at $25 billion.
  • OpenAI filed confidentially for an IPO in May 2026 and is targeting a public listing as early as Q4 2026 at a valuation of approximately $1 trillion.
  • The company ended Q1 with $73 billion in cash after a record $110 billion funding round led by Amazon, Nvidia, and SoftBank.

Revenue Triples in a Year

OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate has topped $40 billion, Bloomberg reported, marking a dramatic acceleration for the artificial intelligence company as it prepares for what could be one of the largest initial public offerings in technology history.

The figure represents roughly a tripling from the $13 billion in revenue OpenAI generated in all of 2025, driven by explosive growth in its ChatGPT consumer product and rapidly expanding enterprise contracts. The company's API business, which lets developers build applications on top of its GPT models, has also seen surging demand as the AI adoption cycle accelerates.

Cash Burn Remains Enormous

The revenue milestone comes with a significant caveat: OpenAI is still burning cash at an extraordinary rate. The company consumed $3.7 billion during the first quarter of 2026, more than half of its $5.7 billion in revenue for the period, according to documents shared with investors and reported by The Information.

OpenAI has projected it will burn through $25 billion this year and $57 billion in 2027 as it races to build out the computing infrastructure needed to train increasingly powerful AI models. The company ended Q1 2026 with $73 billion in cash and marketable securities, bolstered by a record $110 billion funding round announced in late March.

"The company's lack of profitability is likely to face heavy scrutiny from investors ahead of an IPO."

— The Information

IPO Timeline Takes Shape

OpenAI filed a confidential draft S-1 registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission on May 22, signaling that a public listing is no longer a distant possibility. Bankers have been in conversations about a listing as early as Q4 2026 that could raise more than $60 billion.

CEO Sam Altman has reportedly told employees that the stock market listing could happen within the next year. The company is targeting a market capitalization of approximately $1 trillion, which would make it one of the most valuable companies to go public in US history.

The IPO race has intensified as rival Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI assistant, has also been preparing its own listing. Anthropic was valued at $965 billion after a recent funding round, and its revenue run rate has been reported at roughly $47 billion — putting it ahead of OpenAI on that metric, though OpenAI's consumer user base remains far larger.

The Valuation Question

At a $1 trillion IPO valuation, OpenAI would be trading at roughly 25 times its current annualized revenue — an ambitious but not unprecedented multiple for a high-growth technology company. The company only plans to float 5-10% of its shares, and the limited supply combined with pent-up demand could push the stock higher on its first day.

But the path to profitability remains unclear. Independent journalist Ed Zitron, whose reporting was verified by the Financial Times, documented that OpenAI's losses ballooned from $5.09 billion in 2024 to $38.5 billion in 2025. The gap between revenue and costs reflects the massive expense of training frontier AI models and operating the data centers that run them.

What's Next

If OpenAI and Anthropic both complete their IPOs in the coming months, it would mark a turning point for the AI industry — shifting the two most advanced AI labs from private to public markets and subjecting them to quarterly earnings scrutiny for the first time. For investors, the question is whether the extraordinary revenue growth can eventually outpace the equally extraordinary costs.
